title: Second thin-turn completion reuses the previous bot message instead of this turn's chunks
description:
## Bug

A second message on a channel that already has a Luna bot row commits the **previous** bot message body, not the joined token chunks from this turn.

Live evidence from demo CLI acceptance on development (develop @ 4250986): tokens streamed `Hello, Ryan—this CLI stream check is working.` then `bot>` printed `Hi! How can I help?` (the household greeting). Same pattern on a second run. `exercise_thin_turn.py` still exited 0; it does not assert committed body equals streamed tokens.

## Cause (read, not a patch)

`ControlPlane._complete_turn` for a non-completed turn walks `list_messages` in reverse and, if **any** bot message for `turn.bot_id` exists on the channel, calls `_finalize_committed_turn` with that row's body and skips joining `list_turn_chunks`. After the first greeting, every later turn re-commits the last bot message.

Idempotent complete should reuse **this turn's** committed row (e.g. via `turn.completed` `message_seq`), not the latest bot author on the channel.

## DoD

- Gherkin: posting a second human message on a channel that already has a bot reply commits the new joined chunks, not the earlier bot body.
- `turn.completed.body` matches streamed `turn.token` text for that turn_id.
- Demo CLI `bot>` line matches the streamed tokens.
- First-turn greeting path still works.
- No production deploy. ThinTurn-only development if a live pin is required.

Not included: chat UI, production, computer, CLI UX redesign.
